title: Describe the trade-off and the parties

blocks.heading: Describe the trade-off and the parties
blocks.text: A descriptive appraisal separates private business effects from external community effects and compares realistic choices. Explain the mechanism, who is affected, whether the effect is temporary or lasting and how protection could alter it. A clean production option may preserve output while reducing neighbours’ harm, although it costs resources. Evidence can be incomplete, so give a conditional judgement rather than invent precise values for unmeasured consequences. Benefits and costs can be distributed unevenly; a gain to the business does not automatically compensate a resident.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Hela Blocks compares operating without dust control, installing effective control or postponing the project. Control can reduce residents’ dust inconvenience while allowing production, but adds a private cost. Compare whether it works and is affordable; postponement may avoid harm but forgo useful activity.
